network.tdh.impl.metadataDescription: The Rust core, the Rust and Python references, program B, the Lean model and 6529.io’s backend: how each was written, which conformance vectors it passes, and how they are checked against each other.
network.tdh.impl.title: Implementations
network.tdh.impl.lede: TDH-v1 is one written rule and several programs, written separately from the same text. They run the same test cases and are compared with each other, so a mistake in one shows up as a difference in another.
network.tdh.impl.programs.title: The programs
network.tdh.impl.rust.language: Rust, standard library only, integers only
network.tdh.impl.rust.writtenFrom: Copied from the Rust reference and made into a library, with no rule, arithmetic or decoding code changed. Every copied file is pinned by its hash, and a change to a rule must first be made in P26 and the references.
network.tdh.impl.rust.runsIn: 6529’s daily comparison, scheduled every day from October 16, 2026; 6529.io, from the cutover; every validator, once validators run; proof program A, being built
network.tdh.impl.rust.conformance: The 75 vectors of P26’s fourth round (a4db4ae, 1,207 checks) in the validator’s development branch; not yet the 14 of the fifth. The daily job’s version passes the 51 vectors of 0621ed4 (976 checks); the later ones change no value of a real day (P26 §13)
network.tdh.impl.rust.speed: 0.6 s on one core, computation only. A whole daily run also reads Ethereum and links its block headers: 8 to 21 minutes so far
network.tdh.impl.programB.language: Rust, standard library plus a pinned Keccak crate, integers only
network.tdh.impl.programB.writtenFrom: The specifications, the vector files and the design record, in a separate clean room, without opening any other implementation’s code: never the Rust core, the Rust reference or any Python file. It ran the Python reference’s vector runner only as a black box.
network.tdh.impl.programB.runsIn: Proof program B, being built; and, as decided, every validator’s second check before it signs (D125). Not yet inside the validator.
network.tdh.impl.programB.conformance: The 75 vectors of P26 a4db4ae, its fourth round, in the validator’s development branch (October 15, 2026); not yet the 14 added in P26’s fifth round
network.tdh.impl.python.language: Python 3.10 or later, standard library only, no floating point
network.tdh.impl.python.writtenFrom: Written alongside P26 as its reference
network.tdh.impl.python.runsIn: 6529’s daily comparison, scheduled every day from October 16, 2026; any validator, as an optional third check (D125)
network.tdh.impl.python.conformance: All 89 vectors (1,257 checks), at P26 f840096. The daily job runs it at 0621ed4, which had 51
network.tdh.impl.python.speed: 4.3 s, computation only; 10 to 12 s in the daily run, on the Rust run’s input
network.tdh.impl.backend.conformance: Not a TDH-v1 implementation: the specification lists where it differs and its issues, measured by replay and by the daily comparison
network.tdh.impl.written.title: How each was written
network.tdh.impl.written.body: The Python reference came first, written with the specification. The Rust reference was then written in a clean room from the specification and the documents it cites, without opening the Python, and it listed every place where it had to choose: 23 in all. P26 now states a rule for each; the last, the state-read adapter for edition floors, was pinned in P53 §11.3 on October 16.
network.tdh.impl.written.body2: The Rust reference became the validators’ Rust core without any change to its rules. Program B was written later, in a separate clean room, from the specifications, the vectors and the design record, without opening any other implementation’s code. It found that the first version of D131’s netting let steps inside a transaction change the holdings; P26 made netting uniform the same day, and vectors 45 to 47 pin its three cases. The Lean model was written from P26, definition by definition.
network.tdh.impl.lineage.title: Where each implementation came from
network.tdh.impl.lineage.desc: P26 is the root. The Python reference was written with it. The Rust reference was written from P26 and the documents it cites, without reading the Python, and was copied into the Rust core with no rule changed. Program B was written from the specifications, the vectors and the design record, without opening any other implementation’s code. The Lean model was written from P26. The old backend is replaced by the Rust core at the cutover.

network.tdh.impl.where.caption: Where each implementation runs
network.tdh.impl.checked.title: How they are checked
network.tdh.impl.checked.vectors.title: Conformance vectors.
network.tdh.impl.checked.vectors.body: 89 small cases, each with the exact values the rule must produce: zero holdings, editions, transfers inside one block, transaction netting, consolidation carry, burns, FirstGM, floors, boost tiers, rounding ties, malformed events, the input rules made explicit on October 15 and 16, and inputs that must produce no result. Vectors 1 to 18 were derived by hand (18 updated for D131); 19 to 88 were generated with the reference and their derivations checked by hand. A program conforms when it reproduces every one.
network.tdh.impl.checked.replays.title: Differential replays.
network.tdh.impl.checked.replays.body: Whole days run through more than one implementation and compared with 6529.io’s published values. With D131’s netting, the 2026-10-11 replay reproduces all 10,280 identities and 11,130 wallets; before netting it reproduced 10,278, and the two others were explained (DEV-2).
network.tdh.impl.checked.dual.title: The dual run in every validator.
network.tdh.impl.checked.dual.body: Before it signs, a validator is to compute TDH with the Rust core and with program B. If they disagree on any value, it does not sign and raises an alarm. This is decided (D125) but not yet built in: program B does not run inside the validator yet.
network.tdh.impl.checked.daily.title: The daily comparison.
network.tdh.impl.checked.daily.body: 6529 runs the Rust core and the Python reference every day beside 6529.io’s backend and publishes the three results: scheduled every day since October 16, 2026, after the first two days, October 14 and 15, were computed on October 15. The Python run reads the Rust run’s own input, after checking its hash, so the two compare computation, not reading Ethereum. The comparison is a separate tool, three_way.py, in the validator code.
network.tdh.impl.checked.proofs.title: Proofs.
network.tdh.impl.checked.proofs.body: Programs A and B are being built to prove each day’s result from Ethereum’s own history in two different zero-knowledge virtual machines; a minimal Ethereum contract that records proven results is built and tested on a copy of mainnet and is not deployed.
network.tdh.impl.checked.after: After the cutover, 6529.io runs the Rust core itself, so comparing the two no longer tests the computation, only its publication. The independent checks are then the Python reference and program B.

network.tdh.impl.anatomy.title: Inside one vector
network.tdh.impl.anatomy.intro: Vector 36: one transaction sends copies of two Memes to a marketplace and back, and one copy goes on to a buyer. Its addresses and transactions are synthetic. A program reads the transfers and the cycle, and must produce exactly the expected values.
network.tdh.impl.anatomy.derivationBody: All five movements are in one transaction, so each token’s movements are netted (P26 §7.1). Meme 1: wallet A and the marketplace W each net zero, so nothing moves and A keeps its 100- and 40-day-old copies. Meme 2: A nets −1, W nets 0 and buyer B +1, so one copy goes from A to B: A’s last copy, 60 days old, which B receives fresh, 5 days before the snapshot. Without netting, A’s copies would have left and come back fresh: 285 whole days instead of 560.

network.tdh.impl.v.37-pass-through-clust: A to W to C in one transaction acts as A to C, with age carried inside an identity
network.tdh.impl.v.38-pairing-order: Two senders and two receivers out of address order: paired in address order
network.tdh.impl.v.39-mint-forwarded: A mint passed on inside the transaction, and a zero-amount creation mint
network.tdh.impl.v.40-mint-and-burn-in-o: Minted and burned in one transaction: a burn to the zero address credits nobody, one to 0x…dead credits the sink; the mints still count in the editions
network.tdh.impl.v.41-firstgm-netting: Netting inside the FirstGM burn transaction
network.tdh.impl.v.42-batch-repeated-id: Batch events with a repeated id, out and back
network.tdh.impl.v.43-different-transact: Not netted: two transactions of one block, and one position in two blocks
network.tdh.impl.v.44-invalid-underflow-: No result: an underflow before netting, though the transaction nets to zero
network.tdh.impl.v.45-inserted-round-tri: A round trip inserted before a transaction’s transfers: every value stays the same

network.tdh.impl.format.title: How to read a vector file
network.tdh.impl.format.key.params: Overrides of the P26 §10 registry, by name, in the record’s units: cents, micro-units, 10^-4.
network.tdh.impl.format.key.cycle: The cycle’s snapshot block B and its timestamp T.
network.tdh.impl.format.key.transfers: Decoded transfers in P26 §3.2’s form; tx is the transaction hash.
network.tdh.impl.format.key.consolidatio: Decoded delegation events, kept or not; use case 999 unless given.
network.tdh.impl.format.key.raw_logs: Raw eth_getLogs entries with their blocks’ timestamps, selected and decoded by the program itself.
network.tdh.impl.format.key.expected: The values the cycle must produce: H, editions and rates; identity and wallet records (balance, raw, base, boost_c, which is beta in cents, final, and per token); absent records; totals; clusters. Records not listed are not checked.
network.tdh.impl.format.key.expected_inv: The input has no result. The vector asserts only that: its string names the rule it was built for, and a program passes by rejecting the input for any reason (P26 §13).
network.tdh.impl.format.key.legacy_expec: The values under the emulation of 6529.io’s old backend, for diagnosis.
network.tdh.impl.format.key.effective_ti: The values under DEV-10’s alternative, which D121 did not adopt.
network.tdh.impl.format.records: Other blocks test one part at a time: decoding (logs, expected_transfers, expected_events, malformed_logs), arithmetic, the cutoff and whole days, and the registry hash.

network.tdh.impl.checked.difftest.title: Differential tests across four programs.
network.tdh.impl.checked.difftest.body: On October 15, four rounds of generated cycles ran through the Lean model, the Python reference, the Rust core and program B; each round’s findings were settled in P26 and pinned by new vectors, the last on October 16. Since P26’s fifth round, 6529chain’s automated checks also run the Rust reference on the Lean model’s random inputs, and the validator’s run the Rust core against program B on every change.
